Let \(G=X=\mathbb F_2^9/\langle \mathbf 1\rangle\). Since \(d\) is translation-invariant, the \(p\)-negative type condition diagonalizes in the Fourier characters of \(G\).

The characters of \(G\) are indexed by even-weight vectors \(a\in\mathbb F_2^9\), with
\[
\chi_a([x])=(-1)^{a\cdot x}.
\]
For a character of weight \(j=|a|\in\{0,2,4,6,8\}\), the relevant eigenvalue is
\[
\lambda_j(p)=\sum_{z\in X} d(0,z)^p\chi_a(z).
\]
Using the paired Hamming weights \(r\) and \(9-r\), one gets
\[
\lambda_j(p)=K_1(j)+2^pK_2(j)+3^pK_3(j)+4^pK_4(j),
\]
where \(K_r(j)\) are binary Krawtchouk coefficients for \(n=9\). The four nontrivial cases are
\[
\begin{aligned}
\lambda_2(p)&=5+8\cdot2^p-14\cdot4^p,\\
\lambda_4(p)&=1-4\cdot2^p-4\cdot3^p+6\cdot4^p,\\
\lambda_6(p)&=-3+8\cdot3^p-6\cdot4^p,\\
\lambda_8(p)&=-7+20\cdot2^p-28\cdot3^p+14\cdot4^p.
\end{aligned}
\]
Negative type requires \(\lambda_j(p)\le 0\) for every nontrivial \(j\). The first eigenvalue to hit \(0\) is \(\lambda_8\), so
\[
\wp
\]
is the unique positive root of
\[
14\cdot4^p-28\cdot3^p+20\cdot2^p-7=0.
\]
Numerically,
\[
\wp\approx 0.323267128142707.
\]

At \(p=\wp\), only the weight-\(8\) characters vanish. There are \(\binom98=9\) of them, hence
\[
\dim E=9.
\]

Now identify those \(9\) characters. If \(\varepsilon_i\in\{\pm1\}\) and \(\prod_i\varepsilon_i=1\), then \(X\) is naturally the even sign cube
\[
\Omega=\{\varepsilon\in\{\pm1\}^9:\prod_i\varepsilon_i=1\}.
\]
Every \(c\in E\) has the form
\[
c(\varepsilon)=\sum_{i=1}^9 \alpha_i\varepsilon_i.
\]
Thus minimizing support means maximizing the number of even sign vectors on which a nonzero linear form vanishes. The maximal zero set has size
\[
\binom84=70,
\]
attained exactly when one coefficient is \(0\) and the other eight have equal absolute value. Therefore
\[
m=256-70=186.
\]

For the number \(N\): choose the zero coefficient in \(9\) ways, and choose the signs of the other \(8\) equal-magnitude coefficients modulo global scalar sign, giving \(2^8/2=2^7\) lines. Hence
\[
N=9\cdot 2^7=1152.
\]

So the requested tuple is
\[
\boxed{\left(\wp,\dim E,m,N\right)
=
\left(\wp,\,9,\,186,\,1152\right)}
\]
where \(\wp\) is the unique positive solution of
\[
\boxed{14\cdot4^\wp-28\cdot3^\wp+20\cdot2^\wp-7=0}
\]
and \(\wp\approx 0.323267128142707\).
